title: What Is a Bill of Entry (BOE)? Types and ICEGATE Status Guide
summary: Learn what a Bill of Entry is, how to file it, and how to check BOE status on ICEGATE. See what the Out of Charge date means for your shipment.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


For an importer, the Bill of Entry is the point at which a shipment stops being a logistics matter and becomes a customs and finance matter. Duty, IGST, assessment, and release all depend on a declaration filed on ICEGATE. An inconsistency in it can surface as a query that holds the cargo while storage charges accumulate.


Some delays attributed to the port originate in the declaration itself, in a classification choice, a valuation figure, or a mismatched registration detail. Managing it well requires clarity on what it contains, which type applies, and how its status should be read.


### Key Takeaways


- A Bill of Entry is the import declaration that Customs uses to assess the duty payable on a consignment. An importer or broker files it on ICEGATE for assessment and clearance.
- The type filed (home consumption, warehousing, or ex-bond) determines when duty and IGST fall due and how long cash stays tied up in the consignment.
- Clearance status is visible after logging in to ICEGATE. The Out of Charge date shows when Customs issued its clearance order for the goods.
- Errors in HS code, valuation, or importer details can trigger queries, and errors in GSTIN or tax details can later affect the IGST credit claimed in GST returns.
- Cashfree’s PA-CB Import payment gateway lets foreign merchants collect rupee payments from Indian customers, while the Bill of Entry and customs duty remain the importer’s responsibility.


##


What Is BOE? Bill of Entry Meaning and Contents


A Bill of Entry is the import declaration filed under the[Customs Act, 1962](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2475/5/A1962-52.pdf) when goods enter India. It can be filed before goods reach an Indian port, airport, or other customs station.


- **Importer details** : The importer’s name,[Import Export Code (IEC)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-import-export-code-iec/) ,[GSTIN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-goods-and-service-tax-identification-number/) , and PAN, as applicable, with the broker’s code where one files on the importer’s behalf, tie the declaration to an accountable party.
- **Shipment details** : The port code, vessel or flight particulars, Bill of Lading or Airway Bill number, and country of origin let Customs match the declaration against the arrival record.
- **Goods details** : The description,[HSN code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/hsn-sac-code-gst/) , quantity, unit price, currency, and assessable value determine classification and the duty base.
- **Duty details** : Basic customs duty,[IGST](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-igst/) , and cess where applicable, with any exemption notification claimed, record how the payable amount was computed.


**Note:** Beyond clearance, the Bill of Entry becomes the importer’s record of the import for accounting,[input tax credit (ITC)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/input-tax-credit-gst/) , and later audits, so a declaration that is accurate on the day of filing saves reconciliation effort months afterwards.


**Document** **Filed or issued by** **Used for**


Bill of Entry Importer or customs broker Declaring imports and paying duty


Shipping Bill Exporter or customs broker Declaring exports and claiming incentives


Bill of Lading Shipping line Contract of carriage and cargo receipt


##


Types of Bill of Entry


The type of Bill of Entry follows from what the importer intends to do with the goods, and the wrong choice can delay clearance or shift when duty falls due. Three types cover most imports.


- **Home consumption** : This is the standard filing for goods entering the domestic market directly, and any customs duty and IGST due must be paid before the goods are released.
- **Warehousing (into-bond)** : Goods move into a customs-bonded warehouse without immediate payment of duty, which helps importers with uneven demand defer cash outflow until stock is needed.
- **Ex-bond** : When warehoused goods are released for domestic use, this filing records the duty and IGST due on clearance.


***Note:** For ex-bond clearance, Section 15 generally uses the duty rate on the date the ex-bond Bill of Entry for home consumption is presented under Section 68. The exchange rate for customs valuation follows the original Bill of Entry presented under Section 46.*


##


ICEGATE Bill of Entry Filing Steps


Filing is electronic and is usually handled by a customs broker, though the importer remains accountable for the accuracy of the declaration. The sequence below runs from preparation to Out of Charge.


1. **Prerequisites** : The importer generally needs an active IEC and the correct GSTIN where applicable. For direct electronic filing, an ICEGATE account enabled for filing and a Class 3 Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) should be in place before cargo lands.
2. **Documents** : The[commercial invoice](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-commercial-invoice/) , packing list, and Bill of Lading or Air Waybill form the core set, supplemented by any licence, certificate of origin, or test certificate the goods require.
3. **Declaration** : The broker or importer selects the port and Bill of Entry type, enters goods and duty details, links the supporting documents uploaded through e-Sanchit, and receives a Bill of Entry number once the filing is accepted.
4. **Assessment and queries** : Customs reviews classification, valuation, and origin, and may raise a query or order an examination, so responses are time-critical while storage clocks run.
5. **Payment and release** : Once assessment is complete, any duty and IGST due are paid through the ePayment platform, and after any required checks, Customs records the Out of Charge order so the goods can be collected.


**Note:** The Customs Act allows filing up to 30 days before the goods arrive, so assessment can progress while the cargo is in transit. The general deadline under Section 46 is the end of the day before arrival, including holidays. Some shipments have a different prescribed deadline. Late filing can attract charges and storage costs, so the current deadline is worth confirming with the broker.

##


How to Check Bill of Entry Status on ICEGATE


Clearance status for a Bill of Entry is available after you log in to ICEGATE, and the search needs three exact details. You can also open the **Bill of Entry – Job Status** widget and select **Detailed Status** to download the report.


1. Log in at icegate.gov.in, open the **Services** panel, and select **Enquiries** .
2. Choose **Document Status** and pick **Bill of Entry** .
3. Enter the port code, the Bill of Entry number, and the filing date, then search.


After filing, the broker shares an acknowledgement with the Bill of Entry number and date. These details, together with the port code, are all the search needs. The **Current Status** section shows where the filing stands, and **Payment Details** shows the duty payment record.


**Stage or indicator** **What it shows** **What it means for the importer**


Query Raised Customs has asked for clarification Check the query and whether the importer or broker has replied


Assessment Customs has assessed the Bill of Entry Check whether any duty is payable


Duty payment Payment is due or has been recorded Check the challan and payment details


Out of Charge (OOC) Customs has issued the clearance order Confirm pickup requirements with the broker or custodian


The last recorded stage helps show where the shipment stands. If assessment is done but there is no payment date, check whether duty is unpaid or the payment record is still updating. If payment is done but there is no Out of Charge date, the goods may be waiting for examination or for approval from another government agency. If a query is raised and no reply is recorded, check with the broker whether they have responded to Customs. A pending reply can delay assessment while storage charges build.


Public Enquiries 2.0 is available without a login. It shows whether the Bill of Entry data has reached the GST system, whether it appears on the RBI’s Import Data Processing and Monitoring System (IDPMS), and the status of a duty challan. Use the signed-in enquiry for full clearance status. If the main search returns nothing, check the port code, number, and date, and confirm with the broker that the filing has been made.


##


Common Bill of Entry Mistakes and the GST Link


Errors in the declaration can delay clearance, and the same errors can affect GST credit later when reconciling[GST returns](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-return-filing/) . Five recurring mistakes deserve particular attention in any import compliance review.


- **Incorrect HS code** : Misclassification produces the wrong duty, invites queries, and can lead to reassessment and penalties.
- **Undervaluation** : A declared value that understates the assessable value can expose the importer to reassessment, penalties, and tighter scrutiny. Keep the invoice and other documents that support the customs value.
- **Importer details** : A wrong IEC,[GSTIN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-goods-and-service-tax-identification-number/) , or address can prevent records from matching. An incorrect GSTIN can send the IGST credit record to the wrong registration.
- **Missing approvals** : Restricted or regulated goods need licences or NOCs filed with the declaration, and their absence can delay clearance.
- **Document mismatches** : Differences in quantity, value, or description across the invoice, packing list, and Bill of Entry can trigger queries and examinations.

How Cashfree Supports Payments for Goods Sold Into India


Customs duty and the Bill of Entry stay with ICEGATE and the importer, while payment for the goods follows a separate route. Cashfree’s[PA-CB Import gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/accept-international-payments-from-india/) serves foreign merchants selling into India.


- **Who it serves** : Eligible foreign merchants based outside India that sell goods or services to Indian customers and want to collect payment in rupees without setting up a local entity.
- **Payment methods** : Indian customers can pay using[UPI](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-payment-gateway/) , RuPay and other domestic cards, or net banking at checkout, so the experience resembles paying a local merchant.
- **Settlement** : Once a transaction is verified, the funds are converted and settled to the merchant’s overseas account in a supported currency it chooses.
- **Compliance** : Cashfree handles merchant verification and reporting under the RBI’s PA-CB framework and holds the PA-CB (E&I) authorisation it received in July 2024.


For an Indian importer, the practical link is that goods bought from such merchants still need the applicable import declaration, so customs clearance has to be planned alongside payment.

##


Conclusion


A Bill of Entry carries more consequence than its length suggests, because duty, release, storage costs, and GST credit all depend on it. Importers who choose the correct type, keep classification, valuation, and registration details consistent, and check the Current Status page for the next clearance step can avoid some delays that raise landed costs.

##


FAQs


#### What is a Bill of Entry?


It is the import declaration an importer or customs broker files with Indian Customs on ICEGATE, so duty can be assessed and goods cleared.


#### How is a Bill of Entry different from a Shipping Bill?


A Bill of Entry declares goods coming into India, while a Shipping Bill declares goods leaving India for export. Both can be filed electronically through ICEGATE.


#### What are the types of Bill of Entry?


The three main types are home consumption, warehousing (into-bond), and ex-bond.


#### How do I check Bill of Entry status on ICEGATE?


Log in, open **Services** , then **Enquiries** . Choose **Document Status** , select **Bill of Entry** , and enter the port code, number, and date.


#### What does Out of Charge mean?


Out of Charge is Customs’ formal authorisation to release the goods. Once the OOC date is filled, check any terminal or carrier requirements before the cargo can leave the port.


#### Why does my BOE status show no records?


The port code, number, or date may not match the filing, or the broker may not have filed yet. Check the port code first and confirm that Customs accepted the filing.


#### How does a Bill of Entry help claim input tax credit?


IGST paid at customs can appear in GSTR-2B under **Import of Goods** once Customs shares the Bill of Entry data and it is processed. Review the record in the[GST portal’s](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-login-password-portal-guide/) Invoice Management System (IMS) and reconcile it before claiming eligible credit.
